articles.title_orig: Canada and China Strike New Trade Deal Ahead of Trump Summit
articles.title_zh: Canada and China Strike New Trade Deal Ahead of Trump Summit
articles.content_orig:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Xi Jinping have slashed tariffs after high-level talks in China .
Carney reached the agreement with the Chinese President in Shenzhen on Tuesday, ahead of an expected summit involving Xi, President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The deal covers approximately C$400 million ($280 million) in Canadian exports while extending exemptions on Chinese metals until the end of 2028.
Carney said following the meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting (APEC): "We have unlocked billions in new export orders for Canadian farmers, ranchers, and fish harvesters.
"Canada is building our strength at home and diversifying our relationships abroad so that we have the freedom to live our lives as we choose."
The agreement builds on a thaw in relations between the countries that began earlier this year. Beijing has faced allegations of interference in Canadian elections, while the detention of Canadian citizens and concerns over human rights have previously strained relations.
Under the agreement, Beijing will suspend additional tariffs from January 1, 2027, until December 31, 2028, covering C$116 million in Canadian frozen pork exports and C$285 million in fish and seafood.
The latter includes C$96 million in Greenland halibut, C$87.5 million in shrimp and prawns, C$61.4 million in mollusks such as geoduck clams, and C$39.4 million in sea cucumbers.
In return, Canada will extend existing tariff relief for certain Chinese steel and aluminum products for another two years.
Ottawa is also expanding exemptions to 32 additional categories, comprising 23 steel and nine aluminum items, where Canadian supplies are insufficient or unavailable.
As previously reported by Newsweek , China has already extended tariff relief on Canadian canola meal, peas, lobster, and crab until the end of 2028.
Ottawa says more than 90 percent of Canadian trade previously affected by bilateral tariff measures has regained market access, representing nearly C$7.5 billion in trade.
Carney told Xi that the stabilization of trade between the countries showed how they could work together "pragmatically, to solve problems."
"As we look to the future, we have the opportunity to advance in areas of mutual interest, building decades of engagement between our peoples and guided by our national interests and values," he added.
Xi welcomed the rapprochement, describing improving relations as "the right choice" for both countries.
"The important takeaway from the recent course of China-Canada relations is that we must demonstrate mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit and seek commonality despite differences," the Chinese president said, according to an English translation published by China's Foreign Ministry.
The two leaders also agreed to deepen commercial cooperation beyond tariffs. Canada will send a major trade mission to China in 2027 and launch a Canada-China Year of e-Commerce to help smaller Canadian businesses sell through Chinese online platforms.
Air Canada will begin direct flights between Vancouver and Guangzhou in May 2027, while Chinese airlines are expected to expand services.
The governments also discussed closer cooperation on oil and gas, renewable energy, nuclear power, financial services and customs enforcement against narcotics trafficking.
The agreement follows an earlier deal under which Canada reduced its tariff on a limited number of Chinese electric vehicles from 100 percent to 6.1 percent.
The arrangement initially allows 49,000 vehicles annually, with the quota scheduled to increase over five years.
Carney has set a target of increasing Canadian exports to China by 50 percent by 2030 and said during Tuesday's meeting that the country was "well ahead of our schedule."
The diplomatic shift comes as Xi seeks closer relationships with countries unsettled by Trump's trade policies, but he is set to meet the U.S. president for talks in China later this week.
Xi will hold a trilateral summit with Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin in what some analysts have dubbed "Yalta 2.0” after the 1945 summit between former UK Prime Minister Winston Churchill, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and Soviet leader Josef Stalin. Xi will also meet Trump separately.
Officials from across the world, including from Canada, will be closely watching the summit for possible progress toward resolving the war in Ukraine, although the extent to which the conflict will feature in the talks remains unclear.
Meanwhile, Carney warned that Canada could pursue partnerships with Chinese, European or Japanese carmakers if Trump refused to agree to a trade deal protecting Canadian automotive jobs.
"We have the best auto workers in the world, and we want them fully deployed, full opportunity, in an integrated North American market," he told reporters in Cambodia. "That market has become less integrated because of U.S. trade actions."
The Canadian prime minister insisted that Chinese investment was not intended as leverage against Washington, but said Canada would pursue alternatives if its factories and workers were left underused. "It's not leverage. But action, reaction," Carney said.
Meanwhile, former U.S. ambassador to Canada David Cohen has warned that Trump's tariffs could remain in place even if Washington and Ottawa reach a trade agreement, despite growing optimism that a deal could be struck within months.
Cohen, who served under Joe Biden, told Canadian lawmakers on Monday that the two countries had come close to an agreement before negotiations collapsed in August.
He backed Carney's decision to walk away from the talks at the time, arguing that Canada had been subjected to unfair pressure from Washington.
"I think Canada has conducted itself extraordinarily well under a very intense and, I think, unfair set of pressures that have been created by U.S. trade policy by the current administration," Cohen told the Canadian House of Commons Standing Committee on Foreign Affairs and International Development.
"I think Prime Minister Carney has played the hand that Canada has extraordinarily well."
The former ambassador suggested an agreement could be reached before the end of the year or in January, although it could still leave some American tariffs in place.
The former ambassador said the relationship between the neighboring countries had suffered considerable damage but insisted it could eventually recover.
"I am saddened by where the relationship stands today but I really do remain optimistic about its future," Cohen said.
"The ties between our countries run deep and I believe we have the foundation to rebuild trust, strengthen our partnership and move forward together."
Meanwhile, former Canadian ambassador to Washington David MacNaughton, who represented Canada during Trump's first presidency, said the president no longer faced the same resistance from advisers that he had during his first term.
"The fact of the matter is [Trump] had advisers who were sane and were trying to build a relationship that was good for both sides," MacNaughton told Canadian lawmakers.
He argued that the current administration was dominated by officials willing to agree with the president, leaving Canada with fewer opportunities to influence decisions made in the White House.
MacNaughton nevertheless urged Ottawa to continue pursuing an agreement with Washington while reducing its reliance on American trade.
"Let's diversify our trade but also let's find a way to get some kind of a long-term agreement with the United States back in place," he said.
"And thirdly, let us work on becoming more productive as a country because this does give us a chance."
In the latest remarks from Washington on the prospect of a deal, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC: "I am optimistic that we can get trade deals with Canada and Mexico."
However, he offered no details about the negotiations or when agreements might be reached.

articles.title_orig: Trump Kicks Off Asia Visit After US Imposes New Chip Curbs
articles.title_zh: Trump Kicks Off Asia Visit After US Imposes New Chip Curbs
articles.content_orig:
Xi and Trump when they met in Beijing in May
As US President Donald Trump heads to China, his administration has renewed efforts to curb Beijing's access to advanced semiconductors.
On Monday, Washington announced new interim rules that will increase scrutiny of  data centre operators in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil.
The move not only restricts the export of advanced chips, but also access to their computing power, which Chinese firms currently rent abroad to train artificial intelligence (AI) models.
South East Asian countries in particular have invested heavily in data centres to power their AI ambitions - and Chinese firms seeking computing power overseas have been a key market.
But now these firms will need a US government licence to buy advanced chips from Nvidia or other American chipmakers. This allows Washington to monitor if those chips are being used to serve Chinese companies, or being smuggled to China.
This poses a fresh challenge for Beijing, which has become deeply dependent on compute from abroad in the wake of US export restrictions. At least 30% of China's advanced AI computing power is projected to come from renting overseas or smuggling in 2027, according to research by the Institute for Progress , external , a US-based think-tank.
China's foreign ministry called the new rules "economic coercion" and said Beijing "will take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own legitimate rights and interests".
This is also a problem for South East Asian economies where large numbers of data centres have sprung up recently. Some of the firms behind them are accused of helping China evade US export controls on advanced chips.
One of those is Singaporean data centre firm Megaspeed, whose former director Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese spy. Calls for tighter export controls have grown after Nvidia's Jensen Huang admited to an affair with her and resigned as CEO .
Megaspeed, the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia, is accused of illegally smuggling chips to Chinese companies after purchasing them for use in data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
The company has denied these allegations, defended its business as "legitimate and lawful", and said it has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation". It also said Alice Huang stepped down from her role as director in late 2023 and left the firm last year.
The US Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, however, has said Brazil and the four South East Asian nations "present a higher-than-normal risk of diversion" of the chips that Washington wants to keep out of China's hands.
The new measures are aimed at ensuring sensitive US technology "cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centers in third countries," the bureau added. Licences will be issued on a "case-by-case basis", it said.
Batam in Indonesia is emerging as a major regional data centre hub
Countries like Malaysia and Thailand whose data centre roll out has been heavily driven by Chinese buyers could be hit hardest, says international trade expert Naoise McDonagh from Australia's Edith Cowan University.
But the new rules are unlikely to derail the data centre boom as a whole, says Reema Bhattacharya from advisory firm Verisk Maplecroft, adding that investment backed by major tech firms and clearly identifiable customers should "remain relatively resilient".
Singapore was an early adopter of data centres but when it began limiting new construction, investment flowed to neighbours Malaysia and Thailand. Johor in Malaysia and Batam in Indonesia have also approved billions of dollars worth of data centres to catch the spillover demand.
These countries have been offering incentives such as cheaper land to attract foreign investment, including from Chinese tech giants Alibaba and Tencent.
But now, the region could find it harder to get hold of advanced chips.
The BBC has contacted Singapore, Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand for comment.
Singapore said it is "engaging relevant US authorities" to understand the new rules better, and is "exploring how to facilitate trusted access" for local firms. Malaysia previously said it welcomes data centre investment but "will not allow itself to be used to get around export controls".
The new rules also come just ahead of Trump's meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Shenzhen this week.
Beijing has made self-sufficiency in tech a national priority and needs the best chips to build powerful AI models.
Chinese firms DeepSeek and MoonShot have come close to US rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI. So much so that The Institute for Progress estimates top US AI models lead the best Chinese platforms by only about six and half months.
"This is despite US AI companies having significantly better compute access and financing," it said.
Still, China needs advanced US chips to ensure its best AI models are competitive, experts tell the BBC.
The new restrictions on South East Asia and Brazil have taken away "one of the more practical routes Chinese AI developers had to accessing frontier computing power," Bhattacharya said.
But tighter restrictions could also push Chinese firms towards domestic semiconductors and further drive advancement at home.
That has been a longstanding dilemma for Washington, McDonagh said: whether to keep selling chips to China to retain its reliance on the US, or restrict access and risk further spurring Chinese innovation.

articles.title_orig: Nike hosts first investor day in 9 years as it tries to rightsize its business
articles.title_zh: Nike hosts first investor day in 9 years as it tries to rightsize its business
articles.content_orig:
Nike is hosting its first investor day since 2017 at its Oregon headquarters Tuesday as the company aims to prove to investors that its turnaround strategy is yielding success after a yearslong slump.
Last month, the company reported mixed fiscal first-quarter results as it announced a restructuring plan, including layoffs that it said would start next year. It's the company's third round of layoffs to be announced this year.
Nike's net income and revenue both fell during the most recent period compared with a year ago, and the company said it expects revenue to decline by a high single-digit percentage in fiscal 2027.
The new strategy, dubbed Pace, focuses on the company's supply chain and reorganizing into three geographies. Nike said the turnaround plan is expected to deliver roughly $2.5 billion in savings through fiscal 2031.
Nike has been seeing significant sustained declines in its China market, where revenue last quarter dropped 26%. Experts have said the company is losing relevance in the country, while Nike has said it's actively working to win over younger consumers.
At the same time, Nike announced last quarter that it's creating a new global campus in India as part of its new growth strategy, hoping the country will help boost its performance. The company said it was remaining focused on China even as it begins to build out its India presence.
CEO Elliott Hill's turnaround strategy includes improving different parts of the business at different rates based on priority. While it's seen some signs of progress in the North America business, Hill has said that performance isn't enough to offset the pressures on the company elsewhere, including internationally.
The Nike consumer has also been under increased macroeconomic pressure as geopolitical tensions mount and inflation rises.
Shares of Nike have fallen 50% over the past two years.

articles.title_orig: Putin’s prized bridge is partially destroyed in Ukrainian strike
articles.title_zh: Putin’s prized bridge is partially destroyed in Ukrainian strike
articles.content_orig:
Morning Rundown: Trump arrives in Asia amid Nvidia fallout, Putin’s prized bridge partially destroyed, and what’s with all the recent tech glitches?
A key bridge connecting the occupied Crimean Peninsula with mainland Russia suffered significant damage Tuesday, a landmark blow to President Vladimir Putin .
Videos and photos geolocated by NBC News show the partial destruction of the strategically important Kerch Bridge , with one section collapsed into the water. Russian authorities confirmed that the structure had been damaged shutting down traffic and that an emergency government meeting had been called after back-to-back attacks starting Monday.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the attack “an unprecedented operation in response to Russian strikes on our infrastructure.” He shared video in a post on X that appears to show a missile approaching the section of the bridge that was later seen damaged.
The SBU, Ukraine’s Security Service, said in a separate statement that one of the bridge’s metal arches and the road span beneath it were completely destroyed, and the railway section was also damaged, using a “wide range of Ukrainian-made weapons.”
Dealing critical damage to the bridge is a significant coup for Kyiv, as it reels from deadly Russian attacks on its own vital infrastructure, including two bridges in the capital.
The damage to his signature achievement is likely to sour Putin’s mood ahead of the extraordinary meeting this week with President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping . Putin made the construction of the bridge his flagship project, meant to solidify Russian dominance over Crimea, the peninsula he illegally annexed in 2014 .
Beyond its symbolic value, the road and rail bridge has served as a vital supply route for the Russian military.
Asked how Putin reacted to the attacks, his spokesman Dmitry Peskov said a plan will be drawn up to restore the bridge. “There is, in fact, no doubt that the bridge will be restored. And it will be even better than before,” Peskov said.
The Russian Transport Ministry said Tuesday all train and vehicular traffic on the bridge had been suspended after the second attack overnight. The first attack was reported early Monday. “Experts are assessing the damage,” the ministry said.
Russia’s Investigative Committee said Tuesday it had opened a criminal case into what it called “a terrorist act” in connection with the bridge attacks, confirming there was “damage to the structure.”
Zelenskyy said the bridge attack was the seventh stage of an operation that lasted several weeks. He said his forces destroyed air defense systems, radars, electronic warfare equipment and other targets “on the way to the final objective.”
“Russia strikes our infrastructure every day, including bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region,” he said. “We are restoring our infrastructure. But we are also reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began.”
The 12-mile road and rail bridge, which Moscow says is the longest in Europe, has served as a key supply and transportation route into Crimea from Russia, although Russian troops also rely on a land corridor through Russian-controlled territory in southern Ukraine. The bridge was “the main military crossing from the territory of Russia into our Ukrainian Crimea,” Zelenskyy said Tuesday.
The bridge, which cost about $2.7 billion, is also an important transportation artery for civilians. The Russian Transportation Ministry said that in the five years since the bridge opened to traffic in 2018, nearly 24 million vehicles have traveled in both directions.
The Russian-installed head of Crimea, Sergey Aksyonov, asked residents and visitors to refrain from traveling in the direction of the bridge after the attacks. Two people were killed in a drone strike in a district close to the bridge, he said.
Some rail traffic resumed Tuesday, he later added, as he said passengers without vehicles could also use ferries to get across.
The Russian-installed governor of the Crimean city of Sevastopol, Mikhail Razvozhayev, assured residents the city’s supplies would not be affected, and warned against spreading panic. Authorities were working on developing “alternative logistics solutions” for people who need to return home or continue their journeys, he  said.
The bridge has also served as an important gateway for Russia between the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea for ships carrying grain, oil and liquefied petroleum gas.
The passage under the bridge is crucial for shipping through the Sea of Azov, and the collapse of one of its sections could at least temporarily block this route. Black Sea shipping has been severely disrupted for months as the drone war expanded into its waters.
“This bottleneck was previously used against Ukraine, but now it’s a problem for the Russians. It’s unknown how long it will take to remove the debris and reopen the channel,” Emil Kastehelmi, a military analyst with the Finland-based Black Bird Group, wrote in an analysis on X.
The strikes are part of an intensifying exchange between the two sides, hitting critical infrastructure despite the recent uptick in diplomatic activity and American pressure to try and settle the conflict. U.S.-brokered peace talks in Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates last week ended without any significant breakthroughs.
Authorities in Kyiv said Tuesday that two of its main bridges were damaged and closed as the result of overnight Russian attacks, which they said killed two people. The attacks were acknowledged by the Russian Defense Ministry, which said the spans were being used to transport military cargo.
Meanwhile, energy officials also reported new strikes on Ukraine’s power grid across eight regions of the country, as cities throughout Ukraine suffer water and power outages.
Ukraine has, meanwhile, ramped up the number of drones it has been flying into Russian territory in recent days.
The Russian Defense Ministry said Tuesday that more than 1,400 Ukrainian drones were shot down, the biggest attack since the war began . It came a day after the previous largest attack.
The Kerch Bridge has come under several major Ukrainian attacks since the full-scale invasion, including from a truck bomb in 2022 , and from Ukrainian naval drones in 2023 . Putin has previously described the bridge as a “symbol of Crimea’s reunification with Russia and an opportunity for the peninsula’s development.”
The new Ukrainian strikes showcase “Russia’s inability to defend strategic objects that are critical both for the Russian economy and military logistics,” according to analysis by the Washington-based Institute for the Study of War.
“The road bridge won’t be repaired during this war,” Kastehelmi wrote. “The steel arch is a large element which had to be lifted into position in 2017 and the structural damage to the foundations can be severe. Ukraine has achieved a victory with both concrete and symbolic implications.”
Yuliya Talmazan is a reporter for NBC News Digital, based in London.
Larissa Gao is an associate social newsgathering reporter based in London.
Matthew Mulligan is a senior reporter for the NBC News Social Newsgathering team based in London.

articles.title_orig: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip with economic deals and talks with allies
articles.title_zh: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip with economic deals and talks with allies
articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump has arrived for his high-stakes trip to Asia, and took a range of questions on subjects from Iran to Deutsche Bank leaking details about his tax.
The president landed in Manila, Philippines, for the initial leg of his trip on Tuesday and answered rapid-fire questions from the press while meeting with other leaders.
Asked about a possible Iranian threat to Washington, D.C., he said that, if there were an attack, Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before."
The question was about CNN reporting that U.S. intelligence suggested the country was planning to target senior members of Trump's administration with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in the U.S. capital.
"We take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy," Trump said. CNBC has not independently verified CNN's report.
But the president also said he believed his administration was "very close to getting it done" when it came to the Iran war.
While Trump was airborne, the Financial Times reported Deutsche Bank had mistakenly leaked details of his taxes in March 2017, during his first presidential term. The mistake was kept from the White House at the time, per the FT.
Asked about this in Manila, the president said: "I paid a lot of tax."
"They shouldn't have done it. It's illegal for them to do it," he added.
Trump was also asked about Nvidia's announcement on Tuesday of a new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. The company, which reports earnings later on Tuesday, is reeling from the sudden departure of CEO Jensen Huang, who resigned last week after having an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy.
"It's a great company. It's a great idea," Trump said.
Trump is due to fly to Shenzhen, China, where he is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a three-way meeting on Thursday, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit.
He is also due to hold a separate bilateral meeting with Xi. Asked by a reporter if he would have a separate meeting with only Putin, Trump said: "I don't know, but I would, if it's available, I would do that. He's coming. I mean, it's really with the guests. I am the guest of President Xi."
Trump met the leaders of Australia, India and Japan as part of the Quad grouping in the Philippines and the prime minister of Thailand. There follows a dinner with Southeast Asian leaders, before heading to China.

articles.title_orig: Well-known journalist who reported death threats is gunned down on street in Costa Rica
articles.title_zh: Well-known journalist who reported death threats is gunned down on street in Costa Rica
articles.content_orig:
Costa Rican independent journalist Camilo Rodriguez, who had called out alleged ties between drug traffickers and politicians on social media, was shot dead Monday outside the capital San Jose, authorities said.
Two men riding on a motorcycle opened fire on Rodriguez as he was driving through the town of Santo Domingo de Heredia, police chief Raul Rivera said. Rodriguez was attacked at around 3:20 p.m. local time amid heavy traffic on a main highway, Reuters reported , citing the Red Cross.
Rodriguez, 50, had reported receiving several death threats from drug trafficking groups.
He would name drug lords by their full names and claimed to have provided reports to the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration regarding links between drug traffickers and powerful figures in politics and business.
When President Laura Fernandez was running for office last year, she sued Rodriguez for defamation after he posted a video claiming her home had been built with money allegedly provided by a drug trafficker.
"Regardless of the content of his statements, what happened today in our country is a stain on freedom of expression," Fernandez said in a video released by her office .
Rodriguez ran for president in 2022, but his nomination was rejected by electoral authorities on technical grounds.
He also accused his ex-wife of being involved in drug trafficking. She has filed a complaint alleging he sexually abused their children.
The Costa Rican Journalists' Association condemned his killing and demanded "a swift investigation."
"All evidence so far points to the silencing of a dissenting voice in Costa Rica -- a person who published information about organized crime in the country," the association's president, Yanancy Noguera, told AFP.
In recent years, Costa Rica has gone from being a drug transit point to a logistics hub for trafficking, and has lost its status as one of the safest countries in Central America.
Fernandez, who took office in May, campaigned on a promise to crack down on the crime wave, and said she is drawing inspiration from El Salvador's iron-fisted President Nayib Bukele.
Fernandez herself that she has received intelligence reports showing that jailed gang members have ordered her assassination, the Tico Times reported on Monday.
Attorney General Carlo Diaz announced an investigation into the murder, adding that Rodriguez -- who had contributed to various Costan Rican print, radio and television media outlets and more recently turned to social media -- had declined to enter a witness protection program.
Diaz told local media the crime scene resembled a contract killing, Reuters reported.
"We know he was a communicator who publicly identified people for alleged links to drug trafficking," Diaz said. "Silencing someone who reports on drug trafficking or corruption, in this case a communicator, is a signal we cannot tolerate in a democratic society."
According to Reporters Without Borders , more than half of the world's countries now fall into the "difficult" or "very serious" categories for press freedom.

articles.title_orig: US government confirms investigation into tech firm Megaspeed
articles.title_zh: US government confirms investigation into tech firm Megaspeed
articles.content_orig:
The United States has confirmed it is investigating computing company Megaspeed, suspecting it of violating US export controls by helping to ship tech giant Nvidia's chips to China.
In a joint statement, the US Department of Justice and Department of Commerce said they had been investigating Singapore-based firm Megaspeed since 2024.
It comes after questions were raised about the possibility high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.
Concerns emerged in recent weeks after Nvidia founder Jensen Huang revealed he had an extramarital affair , allegedly with former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. US authorities suspect her of spying for Beijing, which China denies.
Jensen Huang resigned from his role as chief executive last week following revelations he had two affairs.
Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and is suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China. The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.
The justice and commerce departments said on Monday that "it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information" regarding the investigation.
Laying out a timeline, it said it began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".
In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia "concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed". In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its 'no sell' list.
Agents from the Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, then conducted an on-site check at Megaspeed that month and interviewed Alice Huang, who was chief executive at the time.
Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed.
The Nvidia scandal has created tensions between the US Treasury and Commerce departments over shipments of high-end chips to Megaspeed.
On Friday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed the US Commerce Department, led by Howard Lutnick, for failing to properly oversee the export of the chips.
Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over his department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.
While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls.
Huang has agreed to testify in Congress, including before the House Select Committee on China to discuss whether US national security was compromised by his affair.
The White House said on Monday it would further restrict China's access to AI chips from firms like Nvidia.
The reported affairs by Jensen Huang created a crisis for one of the world's most valuable firms - a major company in the AI industry and central to the US as it competes with China for dominance.
In the statement, the US government said it would "bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred".
They added: "Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the US economy, and the Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce will remain vigilant in pursuing justice for those who want to compromise America's technological edge."

articles.title_orig: Tech Stocks Extend Selloff as Nvidia Results Near: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Tech Stocks Extend Selloff as Nvidia Results Near: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
U.S. stock futures were mixed Tuesday, as traders weighed the latest corporate earnings reports and awaited new quarterly figures from Nvidia.
Futures linked to the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 234 points, or 0.5%. Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.5%, while S&P 500 futures hovered around the flatline.
Home Depot dropped nearly 2% after the retailer announced a new CEO would take over next week, weighing on the Dow. That overshadowed better-than-expected quarterly results. Disney shares also gave back an earlier gain to trade 1% lower.
Those moves come as investors brace for Nvidia's quarterly report, due Tuesday after the bell.
Nvidia has been tumbling since last week. Jensen Huang resigned from the CEO post Thursday after reports emerged that he had multiple affairs , including one with an alleged Chinese spy . Further, the chipmaker's board of directors is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. The stock has dropped almost 24% this month, putting it on pace for its biggest monthly decline since April 2022 — when it plunged 32%.
"The tape feels increasingly fragile as Nvidia's AI premium continues to unwind and investors reassess the durability of the ecosystem built around its dominance," said Ben Emons, founder of FedWatch Advisors, in a note. "This backdrop has fueled the 'dispersion trade,' gradually eroding the extreme concentration that has defined the S&P 500 and Nasdaq."
Investors will pore through a slew of economic data on Tuesday as well, including October retail sales and import prices. On the earnings front, Disney and Home Depot are set to report before the opening bell.
The 30-stock Dow on Monday slid more than 700 points, or 1.4%, while the S&P 500 lost 1.9%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.5%, its biggest one-day decline since Nov. 5.
Nvidia reports earnings after the bell, and big investors may have shied away from it ahead of the release.
Morgan Stanley analyst Erik Woodring noted that Nvidia "was the most 'under-owned' large-cap tech stock exiting the quarter."
"NVDA remained the most under-owned large-cap tech stock we track as of 3Q26 end, with the gap between NVDA's S&P 500 weighting and institutional ownership widening Q/Q by 22bps, ending 3Q26 at -2.75%, an all-time high. However, given NVDA shares have fallen 32% in the last 45 days vs. AAPL up 6%, it's highly plausible Apple could be the most under-owned mega-cap tech stock at present," he said.
The European Union's executive body on Tuesday upgraded its growth forecasts for the bloc, attributing an "upward surprise" across the first three quarters to a rebound in exports and solid consumption.
The European Commission's autumn report forecast euro area economic expansion of 1.4% in 2026, up from 1.1% in its spring forecast, followed by 1.4% growth in 2027, in line with its previous forecast.
That was despite a forecast of higher inflation pressures in the 21-nation euro area, estimated to hit an average 3.2% in 2026 and 3.1% in 2027, versus prior estimates of 3% and 2.2%. Euro zone inflation was 4% in October.
Energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain "severely disrupted," while freight and insurance costs have risen sharply, and bottlenecks in refining capacity and tight gas markets have all contributed to price pressures, the report said.
However, it said that medium-term inflation expectations were "well anchored," with markets remaining confident in the European Central Bank's ability to maintain price stability following 25 basis point rate hikes in June and September.
Rate hikes by central banks globally, rising government bond yields, uncertain trade policy, volatile stock markets and "concerns about the profitability and financing of AI companies" are all influencing the global economy, which is nonetheless continuing to expand amid strong growth in AI-related investment, it said.
"In 2026, Europe's economy is holding up better than expected. But we cannot take this for granted... We must safeguard our public finances, boost our competitiveness and lay the foundations for stronger long-term growth," Valdis Dombrovskis, Commissioner for Economy and Productivity, Implementation and Simplification, said in a statement.
Nvidia shares were down slightly on Tuesday, ahead of earnings and following days of decline as the company was rocked by Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO.
The chip giant briefly ticked up but was trading 0.28% down as of 5:05 AM ET in premarket deals.
— Kai Nicol-Schwarz, Jenni Reid
U.S. Treasury yields were little changed on Tuesday morning as investors awaited economic data and comments from Federal Reserve officials later in the session.
The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was broadly flat at 5.118%, while the long-dated 30-year Treasury bond was up just above the flatline to 5.472%. Meanwhile, the 2-year Treasury note yield was down 2 basis points to 4.806%.
One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions.
October's retail sales data is due later on Tuesday morning, with economists forecasting retail sales to grow 0.6% on the month, down from 0.8% in September. A stronger-than-expected reading could reinforce the case for higher Fed interest rates.
European stock markets opened lower on Tuesday, after the benchmark Stoxx 600 index declined 0.28% on Monday.
Germany's DAX was down 0.67%, France's CAC 40 fell 0.45% while the U.K.'s FTSE 100 was 0.64% lower in early deals.
London-listed telecoms firm Zegona Communications was one of the few stocks in the green, up 3.8% after reporting higher revenue though a lower operating profit in half-year results due to debt refinancing costs.
Deutsche Bank was the worst performer on the Stoxx 600, last down 4.6% as it grapples with the fallout from the publication of a tranche of leaked internal documents .
Asia-Pacific markets closed lower Tuesday, with South Korea's Kospi leading losses in the region.
Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 1.34% to close at 58,860.43, while the Topix lost 1.57% to 3,840.02.
South Korea's Kospi dropped 2.59% to 4,968.48, while the small-cap Kosdaq declined 2.34% to 650.06.
Australia's S&P/ASX 200 closed 1.79% lower at 8,883.20
Mainland China's CSI 300 ended flat at 3,976.46, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index was down 1.03% as of its last hour of trade.
Deutsche Bank shares opened 6% lower after numerous media outlets, including the Financial Times , Der Spiegel and Le Monde , published findings from a huge tranche of leaked internal documents revealing how the lender grappled with its problematic clients and assets after CEO Christian Sewing took over in 2018.
Emails and sensitive documents show how the bank dealt with years of scandals, which led to billions in fines and legal costs. New information includes that the lender processed almost $600 million in "suspicious payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein," according to the FT's report.
Deutsche Bank told CNBC in a statement: "The matters which are in focus of the media reports date back many years, in some cases as much as two decades. Where relevant, we reviewed these matters at the time and worked closely with regulators."
"In recent years our bank has gone through a fundamental transformation including 7 billion euros of investments in our control environment between 2019-2025. Deutsche Bank is a different bank today and remains focused on executing its strategy which has proven successful, as evidenced by record profits in 2025 as well as in recent quarters."
Nvidia warned its customers that new legislation on Chinese companies remotely accessing its artificial-intelligence chips could expose it and them to U.S. "legal action," sources told CNBC.
The chip giant is facing increasing scrutiny from U.S. lawmakers over Chinese companies' access to its advanced chips, which U.S. export controls restrict from going to China.

articles.title_orig: Tracking China’s War of Words Against Japan
articles.title_zh: Tracking China’s War of Words Against Japan
articles.content_orig:
A headline in the Global Times, a newspaper controlled by China’s ruling Communist Party, about Japan’s “remilitarization” after China restricted exports to Japanese entities. Credit... Andy Wong/Associated Press
By Javier C. Hernández and Gal Koplewitz
Javier C. Hernández reported from Tokyo, and Gal Koplewitz from London.
When China’s leader, Xi Jinping, met with President Trump at the White House earlier this fall, the two leaders toasted to friendly relations.
But in private, Mr. Xi offered Mr. Trump a stark warning about Japan, a U.S. ally, according to two officials briefed on the talks, who requested anonymity to discuss private conversations. Mr. Xi told Mr. Trump that Japan’s recent military buildup threatened to destabilize Asia, the officials said, and that Mr. Trump should be cautious about working with Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, describing her as a “militarist.”
The warning from Mr. Xi was part of a broader effort by China to isolate and undermine Japan after Ms. Takaichi said last year that Japan could be forced to defend Taiwan in case of a Chinese invasion. China considers Taiwan, a self-governed democracy that lies just 69 miles from Japan’s westernmost island, part of its territory.
Since the comments, Mr. Xi has overseen a campaign involving propaganda and diplomacy to target Japan, according to interviews with officials and scholars, and an analysis by The New York Times of Chinese Foreign Ministry briefings and state media. It is all part of a push, analysts say, to persuade the world that Japan is a resurgent aggressor.
China has deployed words and images to portray Japan as a World War II-era enemy, using phrases like “remilitarization” and “neo-militarism,” and videos that compare Japan to a “rampaging gray rhino.”
Chinese officials have repeatedly sought to belittle Ms. Takaichi, Japan’s first female prime minister, omitting her title in official briefings, breaking with longstanding practice. State media has depicted Ms. Takaichi in short skirts and a nurse’s uniform in cartoons, and described her as “Abe’s girl,” referring to Shinzo Abe, the former Japanese prime minister and Ms. Takaichi’s mentor.
In private conversations with Western scholars, Chinese academics have recently pushed the narrative that Japan is the “Israel of East Asia,” poised to lead the United States into conflict and destabilize the region.
Russia has helped amplify China’s talking points, branding Japan as a threat. Moscow has echoed Beijing in describing Japan as an “ enemy state ” that is not to be trusted, invoking a World War II-era designation used against former Axis powers.
Mr. Xi and Ms. Takaichi will cross paths this week at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit meeting in Shenzhen, China. The encounter is expected to be frosty; Mr. Xi might try to use the summit as an opportunity to alienate Ms. Takaichi from Japan’s allies, experts say.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia Forms Export Control Board Committee After Chip Curbs
articles.title_zh: Nvidia Forms Export Control Board Committee After Chip Curbs
articles.content_orig:
NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that the Board of Directors has established the National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, a new standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management. NVIDIA’s existing National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team will report directly to the Committee and to Interim CEO, Colette Kress, on day-to-day operations.
The Committee will be chaired by director Suzanne Nora Johnson and will also include directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri as members. It will meet at least quarterly, including with management and in executive session. The Committee will oversee the Company’s ongoing efforts to enhance its internal National Security Team and Global Trade Compliance Team, and work closely with independent third-party experts in law, national security and global trade compliance.
“NVIDIA recognizes that advanced silicon technologies and the emergence of artificial and superintelligence present unprecedented challenges for national security. As the world’s leading advanced computing company, NVIDIA has both a responsibility and an opportunity to lead the industry in addressing these challenges. We are committed to working constructively with government and industry partners to help establish and advance a robust framework that uses every tool at our disposal to safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation,” said Harvey Jones, Chairman of NVIDIA’s Board of Directors.
The decision to create this new committee reflects the Board’s further commitment to enhance its engagement with relevant government stakeholders, and to demonstrate the highest standards of governance and oversight.

articles.title_orig: Home Depot names Richard McPhail as new CEO, beats earnings expectations
articles.title_zh: Home Depot names Richard McPhail as new CEO, beats earnings expectations
articles.content_orig:
Home Depot on Tuesday announced its Chief Financial Officer Richard McPhail will become CEO of the company, replacing Ted Decker, effective next week.
Alongside McPhail's appointment, Home Depot said Ann-Marie Campbell, currently senior executive vice president of U.S. stores and operations, will become president and chief operating officer. Jordan Broggi has been chosen as CFO to replace McPhail.
Decker, CEO since 2022, had been on temporary medical leave since August. The company said on Tuesday that Decker has returned from leave but is now stepping down from his role. He will continue to serve as chair of the board of directors, the company said.
McPhail has been with the company since 2005, holding multiple executive roles.
"We're not going to change course," McPhail told CNBC's Becky Quick.
He said the company will continue to lean into winning professional shoppers like contractors and using AI tools to encourage sales. McPhail added that while the company faces more challenges now than it did at the start of the year, it is still winning share of the home improvement market.
Home Depot has been pressured by a sluggish housing market, higher mortgage rates and a more cautious consumer. Still, the company has previously said it's seen resilience among its pro shoppers who are still shopping for their home improvement projects.
The announcement came alongside Home Depot's fiscal third-quarter earnings report, in which the home improvement retailer beat analysts' expectations on the top and bottom lines. The company said comparable sales rose 2.2% during the period, compared with estimates of up 1.8%, according to StreetAccount.
Here's how Home Depot performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
The company reported net income of $3.71 billion, or $3.72 per share, compared with $3.60 billion, or $3.62 per share, the year prior. Excluding one-time items, Home Depot reported adjusted earnings per share of $3.86.
Revenue rose 4.9% compared to the year-ago period.
In the third quarter, the company said online comparable sales grew around 13%, which marked its sixth straight quarter of double-digit positive growth for the metric.
For the full year, Home Depot said it expects total sales to rise roughly 4.5%, the top end of its previously provided range. It also anticipates comparable sales will grow around 1.4%, compared with an outlook of flat to a 2% increase.
Home Depot added it expects adjusted earnings per share to rise 2% this year, compared with prior guidance of flat to a 4% increase.

articles.title_orig: "Essentially Worthless" - Disgruntled Fans Are Review Bombing Pikmin 4 On Switch 2
articles.title_zh: "Essentially Worthless" - Disgruntled Fans Are Review Bombing Pikmin 4 On Switch 2
articles.content_orig:
Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is out now, bringing 4K visuals to the 2023 title along with the new Dandori Academy mode and some neat little extras like voice commands.
We awarded it a score of 7/10 in our review. It's still good – hell, the main Pikmin 4 campaign is possibly the best of the bunch – yet we can't deny our disappointment at the lack of mouse controls and 60fps performance.
But if you take a look on Metacritic , you'd think Nintendo just put out its worst game in years. Although the metascore is sitting at a commendable 83, the game's user score is much, much lower at 2.3. This essentially means its average is 'Generally Unfavourable'. Yeesh.
Most folks just seem disgruntled at the notion that Nintendo is charging for what they perceive to be a very minor upgrade over the original. It's true that a lot of games over the years have received free updates for newer hardware, but Nintendo has opted to charge £7.99 / $9.99 / €9.99 .
"This switch 2 edition is essentially worthless. At worst it's a spit in the face of series fans. $20 AUD for a bunch of recycled content and 4k visuals. They couldn't even be bothered to implement 60fps even though the system could definitely handle it. Such a lazy update, and yet they have the gall to charge $20 AUD."
Meanwhile, another user provided a slightly more measured assessment, stating:
"The Dandori Academy has reused content, half of the maps so far are taken directly from the base game and the other half share the same exact layout. Plus the new card on the title screen looks like an ad, ruins the nice scenery, fortunately it can be hidden.
"The main game has also suffered, now somehow having longer loading times than it did on the original Switch. All other Switch 2 editions have made them shorter, so this is really weird. It's not a small difference either, some have literally doubled."
The comment about the load times is particularly interesting.
This has been highlighted elsewhere, with YouTuber 'Press A!' posting an analysis titled 'Pikmin 4's DLC is a disaster...' (flexing that signature YouTube nuance right there) in which he compares the load times of the Switch 2 Edition with the original. When exiting out of a cave, the original would take around 6 seconds or so to load the main environment, however the same moment took over 30 seconds in the Switch 2 version.
A few people have mentioned the load times being quite long, so we tested it out ourselves. While loading into a cave takes about 6 seconds, loading out took around 14-15 seconds. Not the 30+ that others are citing, then, but probably long enough to raise an eyebrow or two.
Pikmin 4's user score on Switch 2 is a startling contrast to that of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . Despite some concerns here and there regarding the game's overall difficulty and approachability compared to the original, Ocarina of Time commands the highest user score of all time at 9.6.
We'll be curious to see whether Nintendo takes any steps to improve the load times in Pikmin 4, but for what you actually get with the new content and visual enhancements on Switch 2, we'd say the upgrade price is probably appropriate. It'll tide us over until Pikmin 5, at least.

articles.title_orig: 80+ PS5, PS4 Games to Buy in PS Store's Updated Black Friday Sale
articles.title_zh: 80+ PS5, PS4 Games to Buy in PS Store's Updated Black Friday Sale
articles.content_orig:
The PS Store's Black Friday sale is on now, running until 30th November, 2026 — and it's just been refreshed with even more discounts.
As with nearly every offer in Sony's digital store, there are literally thousands of PS5 and PS4 games going cheap. Obviously, nobody has the time to scroll through all those deals, which is where this guide hopefully comes in handy.
We've put together a (relatively) shorter list of some of the games we'd highly recommend while they're on offer.
Everything listed here comes with at least a 7/10 score from Push Square , and every game is at its lowest price point, with some setting new lows in this sale.
Subscribe to Push Square on YouTube 172k
Discounted prices are shown in bold , and games at a new lowest-ever price are bold and underlined .
If you need to top up your PSN wallet, we've got you covered:
Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.
Let's have a look at some of the best games in the Black Friday sale.
Offer ends 30th November 2026
The best James Bond game in a very long time, 007 First Light revives the character in brilliant style. Telling the origin story of the would-be spy, the game is a combination of sandbox-like, open-ended missions and linear set pieces and narrative moments, resulting in a highly appealing blockbuster. It tells a decent story, establishes fantastic new takes on well-known characters, and sets a solid foundation with great espionage and action gameplay.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
1000xRESIST is all in on story, and this laser focus allows it to tell one of the most captivating and intriguing experiences you can have in video games. This sci-fi adventure sees an alien disease almost wipe out humanity, but one person is immune, and they rebuild society underground by cloning her. Combining visual novel elements with exploration, it's not the most challenging game to play, but its narrative more than makes it worthwhile.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
If you're looking for a chilled out puzzle game to wind down with, A Monster's Expedition comes highly recommended. It's one of those puzzlers with a seemingly straightforward set of mechanics, but it uses them in increasingly smart ways to really test your brainpower. Set across hundreds of tiny islands you need to navigate by pushing logs into the water, its forgiving nature and gentle presentation make it a lovely game to get lost in.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
A whimsical, miniature open world awaits in A Short Hike . From a top-down perspective, you explore an island with lots of interesting places to visit and adorable characters, each of whom has a task for you. This laid back experience is a true joy as you gain new abilities, collect things, and discover new areas.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
Absolum is both a brilliantly crafted beat-'em-up and a devilishly addictive roguelike. Although the overall experience does feel slightly short-lived, you'll seriously struggle to tear yourself away from the game's striking fantasy world — especially when all of its systems start to click.
Offer ends 30th November 2026
ARC Raiders is a phenomenal showcase of what immersive multiplayer can be. Every run is different, and your squad will come out with stories to tell each time. It can be tougher on those planning to play solo, and the extraction loop won't be for everyone. But as far as extraction shooters go, this is one of the most accessible, and it respects your time, giving you a fun experience from your first match. We can easily say that ARC Raiders is one of the best multiplayer games this generation.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure is a delightfully inventive puzzle game that weaves in a neat narrative to pull you through. Playing as a character that literally moves the world around her as she goes, this is effectively a series of slide puzzles set within a fleshed out world full of whimsical character. Always building on its core idea in imaginative ways, this is brilliant fun from start to finish.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
Building upon the great foundations laid in Astro's Playroom , Astro Bot is the full-blown 3D platformer the little robot deserves. It's an explosion of creativity and fun; there is something new to discover in practically every level, and all of it is purpose built to put a smile on your face. Not only is it bursting with imagination, it's also executed brilliantly. The controls are spot on, every new mechanic and power-up is fun to use, and it's all presented with incredibly sharp visuals and flawless performance. The icing on the cake is its celebration of PlayStation's past 30 years, with delightful nods to hundreds of classics. We can't recommend this highly enough.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
While many of the included games may border on unplayable from a modern perspective, the painstaking attention to detail in Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration is extremely easy to appreciate. The museum-like carousel of content, from interviews through to original artwork, is presented so handsomely that you can’t not get swept up in Atari’s dramatic story. And the fact that there over 100 of the company’s most famous titles, emulated excellently with their original instruction manuals available to pore over, adds playable context to a lot of the content. This is just an impressive overall experience that will appeal to those who lived through the rise (and fall) of Atari, as well as younger players eager to learn a little more about one of the industry’s true pioneers.
Offer ends 30th November 2026
Avowed is arguably Obsidian's strongest modern release, and it's not for the reasons that you may think. While the game's writing and storytelling often lack bite and excitement, its gameplay saves the day with a cracking combat system, meaningful player choice, and the enjoyable exploration of some truly stunning locales.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
Ball X Pit is a dangerously addictive roguelite that combines the speedy runs and rapid leveling up of Vampire Survivors with the ball-bouncing action of Breakout . It's one of those concepts that'll make you question why a game like it hasn't been done before, because it works brilliantly. Every element of the game feeds into something else, and the result is this incredibly compelling game that has a surprising amount to see and do.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
Battle Chef Brigade Deluxe is the definitive version of this unusual but great culinary adventure. Set in a world where chefs go head-to-head in a prestigious cooking tournament, the game is half action title and half cooking minigames. You'll go out slaying monsters and harvesting ingredients, then brew them up to create delicious dishes to satisfy the judges. It's an odd recipe, but results in a surprisingly tasty dish.
Offer ends 30th November 2026
Battlefield 6 is a phenomenal multiplayer experience that immerses and impresses with its chaotic mix of tight gunplay, best-in-class audio design, and the cinematic flair that made us love the series in the first place. The campaign isn’t anything to write home about, and Portal has yet to fully prove its worth, but they act as additions to what is easily the best Battlefield in over a decade.
Offer ends 20th November 2026
A true cult classic, Beyond Good & Evil: 20th Anniversary Edition is a lovely remaster of a PS2 favourite. Playing as freedom fighter Jade, this unique sci-fi adventure has you exploring a weird and wonderful world through the lens of her camera. The remaster brings the visuals up to date and throws in some quality-of-life improvements, but the main reason to play this is for the great story and characters, which remain fresh and charming to this day.
Offer ends 20th November 2026

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang was building Anthropic's worst nightmare. Then he was ousted.
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang was building Anthropic's worst nightmare. Then he was ousted.
articles.content_orig:
Author of the AI Insider newsletter
Jensen Huang 's dramatic departure from Nvidia may be the best thing to happen to Anthropic just as the AI startup prepares to go public this week.
Under Huang, Nvidia was investing heavily in cheaper, more open AI models that compete with Anthropic's offerings. The chip giant was also backing startups developing these alternative models and helping make them widely available.
That threatened Anthropic's business model, which involves spending heavily to develop closed AI models and charges customers to use them, often at higher prices than open alternatives.
"People really need to understand that the 'Cold War' going on here is that Nvidia was on a titanic collision course with the labs," the CEO of a leading AI startup told Business Insider. This person asked not to be identified while discussing sensitive topics.
The executive, who supports the open-source AI community and is sympathetic to Huang, described an ambitious Nvidia strategy to develop its own AI models, invest in rival startups, and build an ecosystem that could challenge not just Anthropic, but OpenAI too.
This strategy was just beginning to come together. But with Huang gone, the threat has diminished considerably.
The timing is extraordinary. Anthropic is preparing for a stock market debut this week that could value it at $1.4 trillion.
Investors are being asked to make an enormous bet on the future profitability of its AI services. Huang was helping build a world in which companies wouldn't necessarily have to pay Anthropic for that intelligence.
The strategy centered on " open-weight " AI models. Unlike Anthropic's Fable and Opus offerings and OpenAI's top GPT models, these alternative systems can be downloaded, modified, and operated independently.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
That makes them attractive to businesses that want greater control over their AI systems without paying a leading AI lab every time someone uses the technology.
Nvidia was pursuing this aggressively.
It developed its own family of open models, called Nemotron. It also backed startups including Reflection AI, Thinking Machines Lab, and Poolside, while moving to acquire Hugging Face, a major platform for sharing open-weight AI models.
Replit CEO Amjad Masad called Jensen Huang's ouster "an attack on open models" at a Silicon Valley conference on Monday.
"Jensen is the premier champion of open models," Masad said. "If it wasn't for Jensen, there wouldn't be a lot of funding going into US open model companies."
On November 3, I watched Huang evangelize this strategy at a Fireworks AI conference in San Francisco.
He acknowledged the value of closed AI models from companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI, but argued that businesses shouldn't have to rely on them. Instead, they could take open-weight models and adapt them to their specific needs, creating AI systems that could be even more powerful.
"By taking an open frontier model, adapting it and providing it with your domain knowledge, your access, your specialized tools, and the proper evaluation, you should be able to create essentially a super intelligence," Huang told Fireworks CEO Lin Qiao on stage.
"And I think those times are here," he added.
This strategy made business sense for Nvidia. More open models running on its chips meant more potential customers.
It was becoming increasingly important as Anthropic and OpenAI sought alternatives to Nvidia's expensive hardware.
In fact, Anthropic has developed a system that could be Nvidia's worst nightmare, as Business Insider reported in October .
Anthropic disclosed in its IPO filing that it has spent years developing software that allows it to shift AI work between different types of chips from Nvidia, Google, Amazon, and AMD. That gives Anthropic more flexibility to choose the cheapest or most effective chips for a particular task, reducing its dependence on Nvidia and potentially weakening Nvidia's ability to charge premium prices.
The shift is already significant. A November 14 analysis by Michael Cembalest of JPMorgan Asset Management estimated that Nvidia accounted for just 39% of future computing commitments by leading AI labs, down from more than 80% of AI chip revenue in recent years.
There was another key area of AI where Nvidia and Anthropic clashed.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has advocated for very strict limits on advanced US chip sales to China, arguing these restrictions are essential to maintaining America's technological lead.
Huang fought against those restrictions, warning that shutting China out would encourage Chinese companies to develop competing technology.
Now he's gone, Anthropic's worldview is prevailing. On Monday, the US government rolled out new restrictions that close a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to use Nvidia GPUs by renting them from data centers outside China.
It's a win for China hawks within the administration and a huge victory for Amodei, arguably the biggest China hawk of them all.
There are caveats. For instance, Nvidia's interim CEO could continue Huang's strategies. Still, the immediate strategic implications are striking.
Anthropic is about to ask investors to bet on its future dominance of AI. Just days before that moment, one of the industry's most powerful figures pushing an alternative vision has been forced out.
For Anthropic, that's enormous.

articles.title_orig: Should Nvidia bring Jensen Huang back, as Silicon Valley's elite are demanding?
articles.title_zh: Should Nvidia bring Jensen Huang back, as Silicon Valley's elite are demanding?
articles.content_orig:
Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Jensen Huang as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.
The board is focused on an investigation into Huang, and is not in discussions to bring him back, said the person, who spoke on condition of anonymity in order to discuss internal matters. Nvidia has hired law firm Wachtell Lipton to lead a probe into Huang's conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets.
Last week, Huang resigned from Nvidia, the company he founded, after 33 years as CEO. The resignation came days after Huang admitted to an affair, and news stories alleged he had an affair with Alice Huang, who worked for a customer and is alleged to have contact with Chinese intelligence, as well as affairs with employees at Nvidia.
Over the weekend, the Financial Times reported that Huang had discussed coming back with allies. Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner told CNBC on Monday that Huang had not discussed a comeback with him.
A representative for Huang declined to comment on speculation on Sunday.
Many in the tech world have called for Huang to return as Nvidia CEO.
An online petition calling for his reinstatement has drawn 180,000 signatures as well as support from major figures including Elon Musk , Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.
President Donald Trump said on Monday that he is open to Jensen Huang returning as CEO of Nvidia.
"It was not put at risk, and our country is now stronger than ever before," Trump told reporters when asked about U.S. national security concerns.
On Friday, a representative for Nvidia's board said it was in the process of selecting a search firm for the Nvidia CEO role.

articles.title_orig: Carney and Xi Announce Trade Pact Ahead of Asia Summit
articles.title_zh: Carney and Xi Announce Trade Pact Ahead of Asia Summit
articles.content_orig:
President Trump speaks to members of the media on the South Lawn of the White House on Nov. 16, 2026, ahead of a fraught meeting this week with President Xi Jinping of China where A.I. chips could be a key issue.
The Trump administration on Monday announced it was tightening a loophole that has allowed Chinese tech firms to bypass U.S. restrictions on accessing the most advanced A.I. chips through third countries.
The move comes just days ahead of President Trump’s meeting this week with Chinese President Xi Jinping, and in the wake of Nvidia, the creator of the most advanced AI chips, becoming enmeshed in an international scandal that prompted the resignation of CEO and President Jensen Huang and a fresh round of scrutiny over the company’s ties to China.
The new rule released by the Commerce Department will require that buyers of advanced semiconductors from certain countries will need to secure a license to sell or transfer those chips.The administration said the rule would specifically impact buyers from Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Brazil, describing those countries as having a “higher than normal” risk of evading current sanctions.
The measure is set to go into effect in 90 days.
China is currently barred from purchasing certain advanced chips directly from U.S.-based companies like Nvidia. Yet some Chinese companies have circumvented the rules by either purchasing the chips through shell companies in third countries, or renting computing powers among data centers located in countries where the U.S. hasn’t restricted on chip exports.
The new rule will also give Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick wide discretion as to which chips may require more safeguards. According to the rules, the secretary may inform a company selling AI chips “orally” about stricter export rules on certain items if the department believes there is “an unacceptable risk.”
The rules came days after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Lutnick for failing to properly oversee the chip exports to China in a CNBC interview on Sunday.
The rare public criticism came after Huang’s resignation as head of Nvidia in the wake of revelations about his extramarital affairs, including a relationship with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of spying for China. Megaspeed is suspected by the Commerce Department of diverting Nvidia chips to China in violation of U.S. export controls, but a month-long investigation by the Commerce Department into Megaspeed was halted last year after a top Nvidia official intervened , according to the New York Times.
“Treasury, War, USTR and State were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months,” Bessent said on CNBC on Sunday. “But Commerce has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes.”
“President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage,” Bessent added.
Both Lutnick and Bessent are expected to travel with Trump to China this week, according to Semafor. Trump is scheduled to arrive in China on Wednesday to meet with both Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Aside from AI chips, the first-of-its-kind summit will also focus on the reduction of nuclear weapons.
The federal government began restricting China's access to AI chips in Trump's first term, as both countries raced to become the leader  in this fast-evolving technology. The Biden administration intensified this policy , making the export of advanced chips to China illegal in 2022. Beijing nevertheless still succeeded in stockpiling thousands of chips to build its own AI systems thanks to an international smuggling network.
Last year, Trump reversed his own administration’s export restrictions, allowing Nvidia to sell two types of computer chip used in the development of artificial intelligence to "approved customers" in China in exchange for a portion of the revenue cut. Those moves are poised to draw more scrutiny next year when Democrats take control of Congress, with both chambers likely probing the Trump Administration's AI policies in the wake of the Nvidia scandal. Congressional lawmakers have asked the Commerce Department to preserve all records related to Nvidia as a part of the investigation.

articles.title_orig: Nvidia stock valuation looks 'draconian,' even without Jensen Huang: Analyst
articles.title_zh: Nvidia stock valuation looks 'draconian,' even without Jensen Huang: Analyst
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
When the forward price-to-earnings ratio on Nvidia ( NVDA ) is six points below that of slow-growing, struggling food giant PepsiCo ( PEP ) — as is currently the case — it's worth checking which financial assumptions are now in play on Wall Street.
UBS thinks the assumptions about Nvidia are brutal and unlikely to be correct, given the chip giant's momentum for at least two more years, even without Huang as CEO.
Nvidia stock rose 1% before the bell on Tuesday.
"In essence, the market is assuming calendar year 2028 will be the peak, there will be no growth thereafter, and EBITDA margins will compress ~1,500 basis points — this seems incredibly draconian to us," UBS analyst Tim Arcuri wrote on Monday.
Arcuri added, "We believe the near-term damage to the stock has been done and we don't think it makes sense to give up on the stock after being down this much (as some of our peers have done last week) especially ahead of January hyperscaler earnings calls where we think capex will be guided higher than current Street expectations."
Arcuri maintained a Buy rating on Nvidia's stock.
Huang was ousted as CEO of the company he founded in 1993 amid a shocking turn of events last week.
According to the New York Times , Huang, whose relationship with a woman suspected to be a Chinese spy has embroiled the company in scandal this week, also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, one of Huang's 60 or so direct reports.
Reuters reported last Thursday that Huang had a relationship with another Nvidia employee, whose name was not released. Huang has been married to his wife, Lori, for more than 40 years.
While Nvidia looks for a successor, the board has installed longtime CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO ahead of the company's earnings release on Tuesday.
Nvidia has now lost about $1.8 trillion in market value since the Oct. 6 peak.
Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya also thinks the stock has gotten too cheap.
"The stock's 11x forward PE is a multi-decade low and a ~36% forward discount to close peer Broadcom, reflecting a considerable amount of stress and potential for rebound," Arya wrote. "Any industry (DC slowdown) or company (China scrutiny, ASIC competition) concern is only likely to manifest in late calendar year 2027/2028. Our modeling indicates $15+ in calendar year 2028 estimated EPS, ~50% above current levels, even if sales flat year over year at ~$700 billion. The stock's implied 7x/11x PE on current/downside remains compelling. Importantly, even a 40% free cash flow rate (vs. consensus 50%) could translate to ~$300 billion in annual free cash flow for buybacks/ecosystem financing."
